explain_note: `explain` per player + `explain_model`: HOW the stack rating was assembled -- scouting-report halves (box wage sheet, plus-minus history), their reliability mix, the aging offset, the wage sheet itemised per stat, and what the tape moved him by; per-36 like the stack fields, `mu + move == stack` by construction. Display fields, no feature token (the value_off_per36 precedent)
replacement_note: 🔴 issue #70 F5, owner decision 2026-09-03: 'I would like 0 to be replacement player.' value_pg/value_per36 are UNCHANGED (average-NBA-player-zero -- pricing.ts still reads them that way, do not repoint it). value_per_game_above_replacement/value_per36_above_replacement are the NEW display fields for a player page's WORTH statement: (his rating - replacement_per36) x minutes, matching the `rankings` board and the mcp_entry PLAYER PAGE surface. replacement_per36 above (bundle-level, unchanged in VALUE from before this change, just newly explained) is the number to subtract from ANY other per-36 rating field on this bundle a page wants to price above replacement instead of above average.
stack_note: stack_net/off/def_per36, expected_minutes, value_pg, evidence carry THE TOP-100 STACK player rating (display fields, no feature token -- the value_off_per36 precedent); pricing still uses value_per36
value_off_def_note: value_off_per36/value_def_per36 (they ADD to value_per36; a POSITIVE def is GOOD defence, the opposite of the team ratings' convention) are what the receiver prices a roster edit from: a man's offence lands on his new team's offence and his defence on its defence, instead of half his net landing on each. replacement_tilt_per36 is the offence-minus-defence lean handed to anybody the model has no per-side opinion about.
